Close the two CT24 findings in r25; no id/envelope changes; blocker if impossible. Round 14 of the reset 12-14 budget (final round).

1 CT24-C5 HIGH (lifecycle hazard): the moved-entry guard keyed on entry identity conflates distinct hard-linked directory entries. Counterexample: snapshot.json is a symlink targeting snapshot.json; prompts.json is a hard link to that symlink (same inode, same target text, different directory entry). Both pre-pass chains loop. Pass 1 quarantines snapshot.json as read_error; prompts.json then dangles and its pass no-ops; D12 records the move by pre-move entry identity, so the guard treats prompts.json as already moved and excludes reconciliation. Admission republishes snapshot.json, prompts.json now resolves to catalog bytes, SavePrompts refuses, restart quarantines prompts again: the C5 self-healing failure recurs. Fix: identify a moved configured entry by its original configured path (plus identity where useful), and decide partner-versus-self from the recorded chain-entry path rather than inode alone, keeping retention protection separate and unchanged. Define the mutual detection with that path-based exclusion, state the ordinary/mutual eligibility precisely, and add the hard-linked-symlink layout under AC2-9: exactly [snapshot read_error, prompts orphaned_link], preserved link text, fresh regular prompts.json accepted by direct SavePrompts, second-run no-op, no missing-source fatal. Show that both-moved and self-moved cases still fire zero reconciliations and the clean mutual pair still fires exactly one.

2 CT24-C8 LOW: spec.md:245 says the fixtures are "still passing under the stricter key" although no implementation exists and section 9.6 declares tests planned. Replace with wording that the fixtures remain required planned oracles; do not imply executed GREEN.

Return the complete nine-section spec, unchanged ids, and a change log mapping each finding to its closing text. Do not claim reviews, approvals, owner confirmations beyond the mutual-link direction, or test execution.
